references.text: Jacob makes a vow to the Lord at Bethel, an early example of making vows (נדר) to God in the Old Testament.
Jephthah makes a vow to the Lord before battle, a similar situation where Israel promises something to God in exchange for victory.
The law concerning vows to the Lord - when one makes a vow (נדר) to the Lord, it must be kept.
The command to strike the enemies with the ban (החרם) - the same term is used here for dedicating cities to destruction.
Legislation on striking cities with the ban (חרם), which Israel promises to do with the Canaanite cities.
Jericho is struck with the ban (חרם), a fulfillment of the practice Israel promised in Numbers 21:2.
The immediate fulfillment of the vow - the Lord gives the Canaanites into Israel's hand, and they strike them with the ban.
Legislation concerning things devoted to the ban (חרם) - what is banned belongs to the Lord.
Hannah makes a vow (נדר) to the Lord, another example of making vows to God in times of distress.
